openQuestions: TWO AGENT STUDIOS: /studio (src/screens/studio/AgentStudio.tsx, prompt-first, linked from the sidebar and the dashboard tile) and /app/build/agent-studio (src/screens/app/AgentStudio.tsx, node canvas, unreachable from any link). They share no data model, no state and no route family. Are these one product in two phases, two products, or is the canvas dead code to delete? The schema differs completely depending on the answer.

STUDIO WORKSPACE SCOPE: /studio/workspace/[workspaceId]/home accepts an id the component never reads. What does a studio workspace scope — agents only, or also knowledge/tables/files/schedules/logs? Is it per-tenant, per-team or per-user, and how does a user get a default one? Cannot be inferred from the source.

MODEL CATALOGUE: four hardcoded lists disagree in both membership and format (chatModels: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6','Claude Opus 4.6','GPT-4.1','Gemini 2.5 Pro','Llama 3.3 70B'; PromptLab: 'Claude Sonnet 4','Claude Opus 4','GPT-4o','Gemini Pro'; vibeModels: 'Default · claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-5','claude-sonnet-5','claude-haiku-4-5'; studioModel: 'claude-sonnet-4-6'). Which models are actually licensed and callable, and which surfaces may use which? Do not infer a provider contract from these strings.

CREDIT ECONOMICS: costs are hardcoded per surface with no basis — suite tools 0-4 by tool, chat 1/turn, Prompt Lab 3/run flat regardless of model or tokens, Vibe build 15, Copilot 2/ask, agent run always 6. Is a credit a fixed unit of currency, a token proxy, or a per-model multiplier? What is the real price list?

ZERO-COST TOOLS: seven tools are priced 0 (hashtag-generator, invoice-description-writer, git-commit-message-writer, task-breakdown, checklist-generator, citation-formatter, alt-text-generator). Because spend(0) can never fail they run on an exhausted pool. Is free-tier metering intended, or is 0 a data-entry error?
CREDIT UNITS: Vibe Studio labels the same number 'AIU' while every other surface says 'AI Credits'. Are these the same unit? If not, what is the conversion?

PLAN CONSTANTS: MONTHLY_CREDITS=1000, APP_QUOTA=5, TRIAL_DAYS=13 are module constants applied to every tenant, and creditsUsed never resets so the 'monthly' allowance is a lifetime cap. What are the real per-plan allowances, the reset boundary, the timezone that boundary uses, and does the trial start at signup?

SUITE TOOL TAXONOMY: two incompatible catalogues exist — businessData.suiteCategories (10 categories / 102 tools / costs 0-4, used by the product) and appData.suiteTools (16 category-shaped 'tools' with different costs: AI Chat 2, Image Generation 12, Code 4, used by the /business-suite marketing page). Which is canonical? Note the product charges 1 per chat turn while the marketing catalogue prices AI Chat at 2.

PER-TOOL INPUT FORMS: Tool.tsx states outright that the live product's per-tool forms were not transcribed and every tool shares one textarea. What are the real input schemas for all 102 tools? Without them SuiteTool.inputSchema cannot be populated.

VIBE CAPABILITY vs SKILL: the product ships 6 capabilities (agent, business-solution-agents, web-app, erp-custom-agents, mobile-app, web-rpa-bot) while the marketing page advertises 12 vibeSkills with a different artifact vocabulary (Agent, App, Web app, Mobile app, Bot, Knowledge bot, Document, Spreadsheet, Deck, Website, Extension). Which set is the release scope, and what does each actually produce?

ARTIFACT SKILL vs KIND: addArtifact writes the same capability display name into both columns. Are these intended to be different axes (skill = builder used, kind = artifact produced) or is one redundant?
PUBLISH PERMISSION: the UI names an 'app-publish permission' that is enforced nowhere and does not exist in any permission list. What is the real permission name and who holds it?

ARTIFACT VERSIONING: publishArtifact sets status='published' AND bumps version 1→2 in one step, so a published artifact is never at the version that was reviewed. Should publishing freeze the current version, or open the next draft? Rollback semantics are unspecified.
TEMPLATE COUNTS: Agent Studio advertises 82 templates and ships 25. Is the gap an unbuilt backlog (keep the target) or stale copy (count the rows)?

FIN BUNDLE: the agent catalogue defines a 'Finance & Accounting' (FIN) bundle with 3 agents but the marketplace has no FIN app, so those agents are permanently unrunnable. Conversely apps PP, PPTX, EVT, RQA and POD ship zero agents while the marketing copy says every app ships with bound agents. Which side is wrong?

CUSTOM AGENTS IN THE PLATFORM CATALOGUE: exactly two of the 60 catalogue agents carry custom:true ('Lead Qualify & Route', 'Resume Screening'). Are these seeded examples for every tenant, or tenant-authored records that leaked into a shared catalogue? This decides whether catalog_agents needs a nullable tenant_id.

AGENT IDENTITY: Run.agent, Schedule.target and PosSettings.agents.disabled[] all key on an agent's display NAME. Are agent names guaranteed unique and immutable, or does this need a stable id plus a name snapshot on every run? (Recommending the latter, but the product rule is unstated.)

RUN STATUS VOCABULARY: the Run type declares 'success' | 'needs-review' | 'failed' but only 'success' is ever written. What produces 'needs-review' — a HITL pause, a guardrail hit, or a low confidence score — and what resumes it?

RUN RETENTION: recordRun caps history at 25 runs, silently discarding older ones, which also decays the per-agent run counts on the Agent Portal. What is the real retention period and is it plan-dependent?

AGENT NODE THRESHOLD: the canvas hardcodes an HITL node labelled 'HITL if > ₹50,000' and a 'Max 12 tool calls' guardrail, and the approvals sample uses a '₹50,000' approval cap, while migration 0001 defaults tenants to USD. Are guardrail thresholds per-tenant, per-company or per-agent, and in which currency? I have not inferred any monetary or approval policy from these strings.

AGENT BLURB CLAIMS: several catalogue blurbs assert regulated behaviour — 'Payroll Compliance Checker: validates statutory calculations against current PF/ESI/PT rates and thresholds', 'Travel Policy Checker: reviews against the tenant's band-based travel policy', 'Contract Compliance Checker'. No rates, bands, policies or jurisdictions exist in the repository. These must come from an explicit product decision; I have invented none.

COPILOT CAPABILITY: the greeting advertises taking actions ('install the Contracts app') and the reply promises approval gating. Which tools may the Copilot call, which actions are 'consequential', and does it act with the caller's permissions or its own service identity?

COPILOT CONTEXT: the 'apragya:copilot' window event carries no payload, so the POS settings panel that promises 'add a field for the customer's region' hands the dock no record context. What context should a surface pass, and is there an allowlist?

PUBLIC VIPPY DATA HANDLING: anonymous, unauthenticated, no rate limit and no consent notice. What is its knowledge source (public docs only?), its retention period, its abuse controls, and how does an anonymous conversation carry over to a tenant after signup as the copy promises?
PROMPT LAB DEFAULT TEMPERATURE: useState(2) against a 0-2 range ships the Lab at maximum temperature. Intended, or a bug that should default to ~0.7?

PROMPT LAB VARIABLES: {{variable}} placeholders are detected and displayed but there is no input to bind them, so a template can never be executed with data. Are variables bound at run time, at agent-binding time, or both?
PROMPT LIBRARY SHARING: PromptTemplate's doc comment says 'saved prompts the team can reach for'. What are the sharing scopes (private/team/tenant) and who may promote a prompt to a shared scope?

ONBOARDING INTENT: the hero prompt is captured into ?intent, displayed as 'Queued for your first run', then dropped — and VibeStudio reads a ?prompt= parameter nothing ever sets. Should the intent become a real first build, or should the promise be removed from the onboarding copy?

MULTI-COMPANY TAGGING: both the tool page and the marketing page say outputs are 'soft-tagged to your active company' and that users may 're-tag or untag' freely. No active-company selector exists anywhere. What sets the active company, and is the tag advisory (as the copy says) or an access boundary?
